recipe_role: This recipe holds calibration envelopes (caps, accuracy, wall, cache) measured on a fixed calibration_model per tier. It is NOT a model dispatcher: the v10 skill-owned executor uses whatever Host LLM the planner is invoked with (e.g., Claude Code's --model claude-opus-4-7). Pass --host-model to inspect/plan or use augment-e2e --model so cost_model.pricing and runtime_metadata reflect the real executor. tiers[].model is kept for back-compat and equals tiers[].calibration_model.

claude-opus-4-7.source: Anthropic public list price 2026-05; Claude Code substrate may apply rebates.

strategy_rules: Use single_pass categorization when rows fit the primary item envelope and text is not exceptionally long.
Use map_reduce categorization when rows exceed the single-pass envelope or text payloads are too long for stable schema induction.
Chunk-level categorization only proposes candidates; final specs must be produced by global consolidation and final selection.

notes: v10 visual preview is a context-compression artifact, not a strict data authority.
Default canvas is high-resolution 1600x2200 with OCR/dense layout to maximize readable information per image.
Raw table/text remains mandatory for row-level tagging, exact counts, numeric calculations, and merge gates.

skill_v10_host_execution.description: Skill-owned runtime policy used by scripts/host_executor.py after reading execution_plan.json. Experiment runners should not override these chunk caps. Effective item chunk size is min(execution_plan.chunking.items.size, selected profile cap), with additional shrinkage for very wide text rows.
notes: 2026-05-28 laptop reruns showed categorization chunks around 250 rows are stable for wide tables; 500-row categorization chunks produced oversized prompts and JSON failures.
Gemini and Haiku should use smaller tag chunks, roughly 100-200 rows, while GPT/Sonnet can usually use about 400 rows.
These caps are skill-owned physical execution policy. Experiment runners should only pass workers/model/query/input/output.

plan_search._doc: Explicit plan-space enumeration used by `plan` and `inspect`. The planner enumerates (tier, ni, nl, cache_hit_rate) candidates, filters by reliability gate (calibration accuracy >= min_calibration_accuracy AND F2 budget OK), and picks the min-cost survivor. Set enabled=false to fall back to legacy first-fit selection.

host_model_compatibility._doc: Pillar 3.A guard. When --host-model differs from the selected tier's calibration_model, classify the transfer: 'calibrated' (host == calibration_model), 'peer_class' (host listed in tier.host_model_allowlist or --host-model-allowlist), or 'unverified' (everything else). Policy 'warn' (default) records the result in execution_plan.json#host_model_compatibility but lets the plan proceed; 'strict' aborts the plan when status='unverified'; 'off' suppresses the check. Override via --host-model-policy at the CLI.

tiers.name: primary
tiers.notes: Justin recipe primary: acc 0.993+-0.006, cache hit 100%, wall about 34s. Caps assumed transferable to peer-class hosts (e.g., claude-opus-4-7); revalidate per host before publishing numbers. forced_fit_rate left null pending real OOS sweep measurement; planner falls back to accuracy_proxy until set.

tiers.name: alternative_large_label
tiers.notes: Justin recipe alternative: acc 0.950+-0.029, cache hit 0%, wall about 137s. Used to widen label envelope when nl > 30. forced_fit_rate pending OOS sweep measurement.

tiers.name: cheap_tier
tiers.notes: Cheap tier reserved for the Section 5.5 planner-vs-static comparison. Routing rules do NOT auto-pick this tier; planner must opt-in via --host-model claude-haiku-4-5 plus an explicit tier override. Calibration TBD before publishing accuracy or forced_fit_rate numbers.

routing_rules: Use primary when estimated items * labels <= 30000 and labels <= 30.
Use alternative_large_label when estimated items * labels <= 200000 and labels <= 100.
Use item x label map-reduce when the estimated workload exceeds all single-call envelopes.
cheap_tier is opt-in only and is excluded from automatic tier selection.

host_model_routing.description: TA++ is a pure-prompt skill: the executor is the Host LLM (e.g., Claude Code). Pass --host-model to planner so runtime metadata and cost_model match reality.
